chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The male slave (mook (male slave) does not combine from among the women more than two wives.
ai.seo_question: What is the maximum number of wives a male slave can have according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar clarifies the marital capacity of a male slave (mamluk), limiting him to two wives, which contrasts with the four permitted for free men. Scholars note this restriction reflects the slave's limited financial means and legal autonomy, ensuring he can fulfill the rights (haqq al-nisa) of his wives adequately. It serves as a key text in Usul al-Fiqh for deriving the specific conditions of polygyny based on social status.
